guards_not_enforced: The runtime load ceiling was suspended while the container-based modules ran. Their workload executes in a container this process did not fork, so its CPU cannot be told apart from a competing tenant's, and enforcing the ceiling would have degraded every such module on an idle machine. Nothing here reports on whether those measurements had the CPU to themselves.

warnings.message: `integer_sort.multi` varied by 19.5% between repetitions (bound 15%). On shared infrastructure this usually means CPU steal or a noisy neighbour rather than a measurement fault.
Multi-threaded throughput reached only 28% of 72x the single-thread result. Expected on SMT and on shared-vCPU plans; unexpected on dedicated cores.
`sequential_write.multi` varied by 36.3% between repetitions (bound 15%). For memory this usually means a noisy neighbour on the same memory controller rather than a measurement fault.
`sequential_copy.single` varied by 41.8% between repetitions (bound 15%). For memory this usually means a noisy neighbour on the same memory controller rather than a measurement fault.

This machine has 2 NUMA nodes. Threads were placed by the operating system, so the multi-threaded figures include whatever cross-node traffic the default policy produced. They are a fair description of what an unpinned workload gets, not of the hardware's best case.
`ttfb.mean` varied by 79% between repetitions (bound 30%). The internet is shared; this usually means congestion on the path rather than a fault in the machine.
The run reached its 512 MiB transfer ceiling, so some measurements were cut short. The ceiling is a hard bound on what this suite will pull from a third party.
`throughput.medium` varied by 23% across repetitions, above this module's 20% bound. On a loopback HTTP measurement that usually means the machine was doing something else at the same time.
